Thanks for linking the related issues.

After reviewing the linked issues and performing additional
investigation on my installation, I believe my case belongs to the same
family of issues. However, I was able to gather some additional
diagnostics that may help identify the root cause.

Database state

The session database is intact.

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session;      -- 5
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM message;      -- 176
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM part;         -- 455

The message.data column still contains valid JSON for both user and
assistant messages, confirming that the conversation content itself has
not been lost.

Example:

SELECT substr(data,1,300)
FROM message
LIMIT 5;

returns valid user and assistant message JSON.

Session metadata

All sessions have:

project_id = 'global'
workspace_id = NULL

Example:

SELECT id, title, workspace_id, project_id, directory
FROM session;

returns five valid sessions, all with workspace_id = NULL.

Workspace table

The workspace table is completely empty.

SELECT * FROM workspace;

returns zero rows.

UI behaviour

Neither OpenCode Desktop nor opencode web can see any of these
sessions, even though they are still present in
~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.

PTY issue

I also encountered an apparently separate PTY issue where every prompt
immediately returned "Interrupted", and the Developer Console showed
HTTP 503 errors for /pty/....

Resetting the Desktop profile by renaming:

~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop

resolved the PTY issue, but it did not restore visibility of the
existing sessions.

Additional observation

This is not the first time I have experienced disappearing sessions.
Over multiple versions I have noticed that:

  Desktop frequently asks me to re-open or select a project after
    restarting.
  Existing sessions sometimes disappear.
  The underlying SQLite database continues to contain the
    conversations, but neither Desktop nor Web is able to rediscover
    them.

Questions

Would it help if I provided any of the following?

  Additional SQL query results
  SQLite schema
  Database (privately, if required)
  Application logs
  A copy of opencode.db after removing sensitive information
  Results from testing a development/nightly build

I'm happy to help test fixes or run additional diagnostics if they would
assist in identifying the root cause.

I’d like to add another real-world use case for this.

My global skills are shared between Claude Code and Cursor:

```bash
~/.claude/skills -> ~/.cursor/skills
```

Several of these skills have:

```yaml
disable-model-invocation: true
```

In Claude Code/Cursor this keeps them available for manual invocation, but prevents them from being exposed to the model automatically.

In OpenCode, they still appear to be discoverable by the model, which adds unnecessary context overhead. This becomes a serious issue when using many global skills together with MCP tools in long-running research/coding sessions.

Expected behavior:

* Skills with `disable-model-invocation: true` should remain manually callable.
* They should not appear in model-visible skill discovery.
* Their names/descriptions should not be injected into context unless explicitly invoked.

This would make OpenCode much more practical for users who share skill directories across Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode.

I’m seeing a very similar issue with GLM-5.2 on OpenCode Go, but in my case the cache sometimes drops almost completely to `0` or `64` cached tokens.

Pricing used:

* Input: `$1.40 / M tokens`
* Output: `$4.40 / M tokens`
* Cached read: `$0.26 / M tokens`

Observed logs:

| Request | UTC time             | Input tokens | Cached read tokens | Output tokens | Reasoning tokens |    Cost |
| ------- | -------------------- | -----------: | -----------------: | ------------: | ---------------: | ------: |
| 1       | 2026-06-29 19:21 UTC |       111300 |                  0 |          1931 |                0 | $0.1643 |
| 2       | 2026-06-29 19:21 UTC |         2515 |             111232 |          1478 |                0 | $0.0389 |
| 3       | 2026-06-29 19:21 UTC |       115741 |                  0 |           177 |                0 | $0.1628 |
| 4       | 2026-06-29 19:22 UTC |       115926 |                  0 |           806 |                0 | $0.1658 |
| 5       | 2026-06-29 19:22 UTC |       116738 |                  0 |           513 |                0 | $0.1657 |
| 6       | 2026-06-29 19:22 UTC |       117751 |                 64 |           146 |                0 | $0.1655 |
| 7       | 2026-06-29 19:22 UTC |         2946 |             115200 |           203 |                0 | $0.0350 |

The key point is that request 2 and request 7 both show normal cache hits, with around `111k–115k` cached tokens. However, the requests in between suddenly drop to `0` or `64` cached tokens.

This happened within roughly one minute, from `2026-06-29 19:21 UTC` to `2026-06-29 19:22 UTC`, so it does not look like a normal cache TTL expiration.

It also does not look like the prompt is inherently uncacheable. The cache can work and then recover later in the same session, but it intermittently fails for several turns.

Cost impact:

* Actual cost of the 4 abnormal turns: about `$0.6599`
* Estimated cost if cache had stayed stable: about `$0.1408`
* Extra cost: about `$0.5191`
* Cost increase on affected turns: about `4.69x`

Excluding the initial cold request:

* Actual cost: about `$0.7338`
* Expected cost with stable cache: about `$0.2147`
* Overall increase after warmup: about `3.42x`

This seems consistent with the issue described here, but the impact is even more severe in this case because cached tokens sometimes drop from ~115k to almost 0.

Thanks for the duplicate check. I reviewed both issues, and I think this request is related but not exactly the same.

#28485 is mainly about hierarchical skill trees / subdirectory discovery control. It asks for finer control over how deeply OpenCode discovers nested `SKILL.md` files, so large skill trees do not get expanded into context. My request is not about subdirectory traversal or HST behavior.

#29462 is closer, but it is broader: it focuses on the `skill` tool enumerating all discovered skills into `<available_skills>` with no upper bound, and suggests multiple possible solutions such as `hidden: true`, max prompt caps, pagination, or lazy loading.

My request is narrower and specifically about compatibility with an existing frontmatter field already supported by Claude Code and Cursor:

Claude Code docs:
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#control-who-invokes-a-skill

Cursor docs:
https://cursor.com/docs/skills#disabling-automatic-invocation

The field is:

```yaml
disable-model-invocation: true
```

Expected behavior:

* OpenCode should still discover/install the skill.
* The skill should remain manually invokable.
* But it should not be exposed to the model for automatic invocation.
* Its name/description should not be injected into model-visible skill discovery/context unless explicitly invoked.

This is important because many shared skill libraries already use `disable-model-invocation: true`. For users sharing the same skills across Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode, supporting this existing field avoids having to fork, duplicate, or rewrite skill directories.

So while #29462 overlaps conceptually, this issue is specifically asking for `disable-model-invocation: true` compatibility, not a general cap/pagination/lazy-loading mechanism.

r u using any plugins? Is this in normal vanilla opencode?

> r u using any plugins? Is this in normal vanilla opencode?

Yes, I’m using the `oh-my-openagent` plugin.

I have not tested this with completely vanilla opencode yet. However, with the same OpenCode Go gateway and the same general setup, `deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` have normal cache behavior on my side.

So my guess is that this issue is probably not caused by the plugin. If it were plugin-related, I would expect similar cache drops with the DeepSeek models through the same gateway as well, but I’m only seeing this behavior with `glm-5.2` so far.

I have not tested whether `glm-5.1` or `glm-5` have the same issue myself, but I noticed another issue mentioning similar cache behavior with `glm-5.1`, so my guess is that this may affect the GLM model family more broadly.

I’m adding two more screenshots from my New API gateway logs for easier comparison. The first screenshot is `glm-5.2`. It shows multiple requests where the cache line is missing, which means there were no cached read tokens reported for those requests. There is also one request where the cache read is only `64` tokens, even though nearby requests are around `67k–68k` input tokens. The second screenshot is `deepseek-v4-pro` through the same New API gateway. In contrast, cache reads look stable there, with most requests showing cached tokens close to the input size. So this still looks more like a GLM-specific cache issue rather than a general plugin or gateway issue, because DeepSeek models through the same New API gateway appear to cache normally.
